questions.question: A school teacher asks students to stand up every time national anthem is sung. Which Article enshrines this fundamental duty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 (a).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental duty to respect the national anthem is enshrined in **Article 51A(a) **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article is part of the Fundamental Duties listed in Part IVA, which were added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• Article 51A(a) states that it is the duty of every citizen of India:
 
 
• "To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem."
 
 
 
• In addition to being enshrined in Article 51A(a) of the Constitution, the obligation to respect the National Anthem is also reinforced by the Supreme Court of India. In its 2005 ruling in the** Bijoe Emmanuel vs. State of Kerala case.**
 
• The **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971** also provides guidelines on respecting the National Anthem and Flag. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** All the Fundamental Duties as per Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, which was added by the** 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 

 Article
 Fundamental Duty
 
 
 
 

 51A(a)
 To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
 

 51A(b)
 To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
 

 51A(c)
 To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
 

 51A(d)
 To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
 

 51A(e)
 To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
 

 51A(f)
 To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
 

 51A(g)
 To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
 

 51A(h)
 To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
 

 51A(i)
 To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
 

 51A(j)
 To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity, so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
 

 51A(k)
 To provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years and ensure that they receive this education (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__****Article 51**

**Promotion of international peace and security:**

 
• The State shall—
 
 
• (a) promote international peace and security;
 
• (b) maintain just and honorable relations between nations;
 
• (c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organized peoples with one another; and
 
• (d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: There is a legal sanction against their violation.
They are part of the Indian tradition.
They are not sacrosanct or permanent.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** There is a legal sanction against their violation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution **do not **have a **legal sanction** against their violation.
 
• They are **non-enforceable** in nature.
 
• Fundamental duties are a part of the** Indian tradition**, as they reflect the values and principles that have been upheld by Indian society for centuries.
 
• Through the **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976,** the essential responsibilities of citizens were enumerated in this constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental duties are **indeed civic duties **that citizens are expected to perform.

 
 
• These duties include respecting the** national flag **and the **Constitution**, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony and brotherhood among all people, etc.
 
 
 
• Fundamental duties are based on** Indian tradition and culture.** 
 
 
• They reflect the** values and principles** that have been upheld by Indian society for centuries.
 
 
 
• Fundamental duties are **not sacrosanct or permanent.** 
 
 
• They can be **amended or repealed** by the Parliament if necessary.

questions.question: All historical monuments have signages with instructions that public should not write on the walls. To which fundamental duty does the given statement belong?

options.text: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood
To defend the country and render national service

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To safeguard public property and to abjure violence**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To safeguard public property and to abjure violence** is one of the fundamental duties listed in Article 51A of the Constitution of India.
 
• Writing on the walls of historical monuments is considered defacement and disrespect of public property, thus citizens are instructed to refrain from such actions.
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of protecting and preserving public property and maintaining a civil and respectful attitude towards national heritage.
 
• It also aligns with the broader objective of promoting a sense of responsibility and discipline among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following duties is specified as the 10th Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To provide opportunities for education to his child or as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 10th Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution is **to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity** so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of continuous improvement and personal as well as collective growth.
 
• It encourages citizens to work towards the betterment of the country in every possible way.
 
• This duty is aimed at fostering a culture of excellence in various fields such as education, science, technology, and other spheres of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties are enshrined in Article 51A of the Constitution and aim to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among the citizens.
 
• Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were listed. An 11th duty was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, which mandates that parents or guardians provide opportunities for education to their children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation. However, they serve as a constant reminder to citizens to act responsibly and contribute to the nation's well-being.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the feature of Fundamental Duties provided under the Constitution of India?

options.text: Duties are inspired from erstwhile USSR
Duties are non- justiciable in nature
Duties are enforceable by the law
Duties are intended to secure the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Duties are enforceable by the law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, which was inspired by the Constitution of erstwhile USSR.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law.
 
• The primary purpose of Fundamental Duties is to remind the citizens of their moral obligations towards the country and promote a sense of discipline and commitment among them.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to secure the country by encouraging responsible behavior among its citizens and fostering a spirit of patriotism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution, and one more was added by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002, bringing the total to 11.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A of the Constitution and are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to contribute towards the nation's welfare.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature**
 
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable and can be enforced by the courts, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable.
 
• This means that no legal action can be taken against an individual for not following these duties.
 
• However, these duties act as moral obligations and guide the citizens in their conduct.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Constitution.
 
• It introduced several changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble, among others.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee**
 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was appointed by the government in 1976 to make recommendations on Fundamental Duties.
 
• Based on its recommendations, the Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

questions.question: Fundamental duties were introduced in Part IVA of the Constitution by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Forty-second Amendment Act, 1976.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Forty-second Amendment Act, enacted in 1976 during the **Emergency period**, introduced Fundamental Duties in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 51A** outlines **Eleven** Fundamental Duties that citizens are expected to perform.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was influenced by the provisions in the **Soviet Constitution.**
 
• Fundamental Duties in India are** not enforceable** by the courts, meaning citizens cannot be legally punished for not following them; they are moral responsibilities rather than legal obligations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Year
 Key Features
 
 
 
 

 **1951**
 **First Amendment**: Added restrictions on freedom of speech and allowed land reforms.
 
 

 **1976**
 **Forty-second Amendment:** Introduced Fundamental Duties and altered the preamble.
 
 

 **1978**
 **Forty-fourth Amendment: **Restored the balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs; reduced preventive detention powers.
 
 

 **1985**
 **Eighty-third Amendment: **Provided for the reservation of seats for SC and ST in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
 
 

 **1992**
 **Seventy-third Amendment: **Strengthened Panchayati Raj institutions for local self-government in rural areas.
 
 

 **2002**
 **Eighty-sixth Amendment:** Made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
 

 **2019**
 **One Hundred and First Amendment:** Enhanced reservation for the economically weaker sections among the general category.

questions.question: The committee to 'Operationalise the Suggestions to Teach Fundamental Duties to the Citizens of the Country' is popularly known as the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J S Verma Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** J S Verma Committee:-**

 
 
• **The committee to 'Operationalise the Suggestions to Teach Fundamental Duties to the Citizens of the Country' was J S Verma Committee.**
 
• It was chaired by Justice J.S. Verma and was appointed by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in 1998.
 
• The committee made a number of recommendations on how to teach fundamental duties to citizens of all ages, including through school curricula, public awareness campaigns, and government programs.
 
• The J.S. Verma Committee's report also made a number of recommendations on other issues, such as reforming the police and the criminal justice system, and addressing the root causes of violence against women.
 
• These recommendations have not been fully implemented, but they continue to be relevant and important.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **L.P. Singh Committee:-**

 
 
• It was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 1978 **to examine the role and functioning of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW).**
 
• The committee was headed by L.P. Singh, a former Director General of Police of Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Abhijit Sen Committee:-**
 
 
• It was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 2007 **to study the impact of futures trading on agricultural commodity prices.**
 
• The committee was headed by Abhijit Sen, a well-known economist and former member of the Planning Commission of India.
 
 
 
• **Paul Appleby Committee:-**
 
 
• It was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 1953 **to study and recommend reforms in the Indian administrative system.**

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment in the year:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties of Citizens were introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act in the year **1976**.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the period of Emergency in India (1975-1977).
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, ten Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was passed during the period of Emergency under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• Besides introducing Fundamental Duties, it also made significant changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, and the structure of the Parliament and Judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• These duties are intended to remind citizens of their moral obligations towards the nation and fellow citizens.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added one more duty, making the total count eleven.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was constituted in 1976 to make recommendations for the inclusion of Fundamental Duties and other constitutional changes.
 
• It was headed by Swaran Singh, a senior Congress leader and former Union Minister.
 
• The committee's recommendations led to the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Emergency (1975-1977):**
 
 
• It was a 21-month period when President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, upon the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, declared a state of emergency across the country.
 
• During this period, civil liberties were suspended, and many political opponents were imprisoned.
 
• This period saw significant constitutional changes, including the 42nd Amendment Act.

__

• The amendment added ten Fundamental Duties to Part IV-A of the Constitution. These duties were considered to be complementary to the Fundamental Rights, which had been included in the Constitution at its inception in 1950.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to remind citizens of their obligations to the nation and to each other. They are not legally enforceable, but they are considered to be important moral and ethical principles.
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2002, added another Fundamental Duty, bringing the total to eleven.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The eleven Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens:**

 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• Honour the motherland and its rich heritage, culture and traditions.
 
• Promote harmony and national integration and the respect for different religions, languages and cultures.
 
• Render selfless service to the country and to put nation above self.
 
• Protect public property and abjure violence.
 
• Strive to achieve excellence in all spheres individual activity.
 
• Pay taxes honestly and contribute to public savings.
 
• Protect and improve the natural environment and forests, lakes, mountains and rivers.
 
• Have compassion for living creatures.
 
• Uphold the dignity of women and children against exploitation and abuse.
 
• Provide opportunities for education to his children, as it is the fundamental duty of each parent or guardian.

questions.question: The celebration of Christmas, Eid, and Holi in school is an example of making children learn fundamental duties as well. Which of the following fundamental duties advocates about this type of ideals?

options.text: To defend the country and render national service
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Celebrating festivals **of different religions in school promotes the idea of** unity in diversity,** which is the essence of promoting **harmony and common brotherhood.**
 
• By participating in these celebrations, children learn to respect and appreciate different cultures and religions, which is important for building a **cohesive society.**
 
• This fundamental duty also promotes the idea of** secularism,** which is a key feature of our constitution.
 
• By learning about different festivals, children also learn about the** history and traditions** associated with them, which is a form of cultural education.

• "To defend the country and render national service," is related to the duty of citizens to protect the **sovereignty, integrity, and security** of the country.

 
 
• This includes serving in the armed forces, volunteering for national service, and being prepared to** defend** the country in times of crisis.
 
 
 
• "To develop the scientific temper," is about the duty of citizens to have a** rational and scientific outlook **towards life.
 
 
• This includes promoting** scientific research**, fostering a** spirit of inquiry,** and rejecting superstitions and blind faith.
 
 
 
• "To safeguard public property and to abjure violence," is about the duty of citizens to** respect public property **and to refrain from using violence as a means of achieving their goals.
 
 
• This includes protecting public property from **damage or destruction,** and resolving conflicts through peaceful means.
